QEMU runs on Redox but lacks KVM-like acceleration, so it is very slow
Initial NUMA support, ARM64 multi-core support, and dual boot from Linux
articles.whyItMatters: Developers following alternative operating systems can see how Redox, the Rust-based OS, is closing feature gaps with Linux.

articles.title: Jeff Geerling announces HomelabFest, St. Louis, September 2027
articles.author: jeff@jeffgeerling.com (Jeff Geerling)
articles.brief: Jeff Geerling is launching HomelabFest, a conference for the homelab community, set for September 12-14, 2027 in St. Louis (technically St. Charles). He is inviting content creators, self-hosting companies, and attendees, with 250 'Super Early Bird' tickets at $100.
keyPoints: Event runs September 12-14, 2027 in St. Charles, near St. Louis
Focus areas include networking, mini racks, servers, 3D printing, self-hosted software
250 Super Early Bird tickets at $100; community tables offered near cost
articles.whyItMatters: Homelab enthusiasts and self-hosting fans get a first dedicated in-person gathering organized by a prominent community figure.

articles.title: Linux 7.2.8 and 6.18.54 stable kernels released
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: Greg Kroah-Hartman announced the 7.2.8 and 6.18.54 stable kernel releases. Both contain important fixes throughout the tree, and users are advised to upgrade.
articles.whyItMatters: Administrators and users tracking stable kernels should plan to update.

articles.title: A summary from the 2026 Git Contributors' Summit
articles.author: corbet
articles.brief: Johannes Schindelin has posted a detailed summary of the 2026 Git Contributors' Summit discussions. Topics include Git 3.0, the security process, documentation, the pluggable object database, and use of LLMs.
articles.whyItMatters: Git contributors and users interested in the project's direction will find the summit outcomes relevant.

articles.title: Phoronix: Linux kernel builds approach the 10-second mark
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Phoronix reports that defconfig x86_64 kernel builds now take about 15-20 seconds on high-end dual EPYC hardware, with 10 seconds in sight. Lorenzo Stoakes' AI-assisted kbuild patch series, now at v4, cuts build times ~36% (and incremental builds ~70%) by removing parallelism bottlenecks, and may land in Linux 7.4.
keyPoints: Stoakes' kbuild patches make kernel builds ~36% faster, incremental builds ~70% faster
Dual EPYC 9754 server defconfig build dropped from 28 to 20 seconds
allmodconfig builds now drop under two minutes
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel developers and anyone bisecting or building kernels benefit from dramatically faster clean and incremental builds, even on non-flagship hardware.

articles.title: Security updates for Friday
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: LWN's roundup of security updates published September 24-25, 2026, covering AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, Slackware, SUSE, and Ubuntu. Notable updates include kernel fixes across several distributions, plus curl, expat, openssl, unbound, squid, and webkitgtk patches.
keyPoints: Kernel updates for AlmaLinux 8, SUSE, and multiple Ubuntu releases
Ubuntu patched curl, expat, gdal, libpcap, and kernel packages across many LTS releases
SUSE and openSUSE issued a large batch including chromium, libsoup, libx11, and rabbitmq-server
articles.whyItMatters: System administrators should scan this list for packages running on their systems and apply relevant patches.

articles.title: systemd Gets Built-In System Reporting With systemd-report
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: systemd is gaining a reporting subsystem called systemd-report that collects static system facts and dynamic runtime metrics into a single timestamped, optionally signed JSON report. Reports can be uploaded to a central HTTPS server on a timer or on boot, reboot, and shutdown events, targeting fleet management.
keyPoints: Gathers system facts and runtime metrics via a generic Varlink interface into one JSON report
Supports three signing methods: local software key, TPM quote, or CPU TSM quote
Periodic or event-triggered HTTPS PUT uploads for remote fleet management
articles.whyItMatters: Admins managing large Linux fleets get a signed, snapshot-based reporting framework built into systemd instead of separate monitoring agents.

articles.title: Dutch Government Builds NixOS-Based Desktop After Microsoft Cut Off the ICC
articles.author: Sourav Rudra
articles.brief: After US sanctions cut the ICC prosecutor off from Microsoft services, the Dutch government launched DAWO, a sovereign digital work environment built on NixOS. The framework covers OS, office suite, collaboration, cloud, and AI, with eight municipalities running pilots and a stable release planned for next year.
keyPoints: DAWO is a full sovereign stack covering OS, office suite, cloud, and AI
NixOS chosen as a Dutch project; openSUSE and Fedora rejected over US commercial ties
Pilots run on decommissioned laptops; 80-90% of configuration carries between deployments
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users and open-source advocates should care: a national government is standardizing on NixOS specifically to escape US vendor dependency.

articles.title: Patches Posted For Enabling NVMe On All Apple M3 SoCs With Linux
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Janne Grunau posted a seven-patch series enabling NVMe storage on all Apple M3, M3 Pro, Max, and Ultra devices under Linux. The NVMe works as on M2 Pro/Max/Ultra, but needs ~140 lines of Device Tree and YAML additions. The patches may land in the Linux 7.4 merge window.
keyPoints: Seven-patch series enables NVMe across all Apple M3 variants
Requires ~140 lines of Device Tree and YAML additions
May make the Linux 7.4 merge window; M3 users should use Asahi Linux meanwhile
articles.whyItMatters: Developers and users running Linux on Apple M3 hardware need mainline NVMe support for usable storage.

articles.title: AMD Linux patches improve HDMI 2.1 reliability ahead of Linux 7.4
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: AMD sent out new AMDGPU Display Core patches fixing HDMI 2.1 reliability issues, such as skipping FRL status polling when the link is down and aligning LT timeout with the HDMI spec. This comes ahead of Linux 7.4, where HDMI 2.1 will be enabled by default with FreeSync, VRR, and ALLM.
keyPoints: Fix skips HDMI FRL status polling when link is down, avoiding blank displays on hot-plug
HDMI 2.1 LT timeout fix aligns with spec; FRL polling serialized against link detect
Patches also advance DCN 4.2 and DCN 6.0 support; DCN 6 likely tied to next-gen RDNA5 GPUs
articles.whyItMatters: AMD GPU users on Linux with HDMI 2.1 displays should care, as these fixes reduce display failures ahead of default HDMI 2.1 support in Linux 7.4.

articles.title: Last call for Phoronix Premium autumn sale: $35/year or $160 lifetime
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Phoronix's autumn Premium sale ends Sunday, 27 September, offering ad-free subscriptions at $35/year (normally $45) or $160 lifetime (normally $250). The site says Premium revenue funds its Linux hardware reviews and benchmarks, noting that under 1% of readers subscribe while most ads are blocked.
keyPoints: Sale ends end of day Sunday, 27 September, any timezone
$35/year instead of $45; $160 lifetime instead of $250
Premium includes ad-free reading, single-page articles, dark mode, priority feedback
articles.whyItMatters: Regular Phoronix readers who want to support independent Linux hardware coverage can get the discounted rate this weekend.

articles.title: Go's expanding SIMD support adds platform-independent interface
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: A new Go.dev blog post details Go's experimental SIMD support, introduced in Go 1.26 for x86_64 AVX and expanded in Go 1.27 to ARM64 NEON plus a portable, platform- and size-agnostic interface modeled on Google's Highway library. Go 1.28 plans to add Arm SVE support and more SIMD operations.
keyPoints: Go 1.26 added experimental SIMD APIs targeting x86_64 AVX
SIMD package covers AVX, AVX2, AVX-512, ARM NEON, and WASM SIMD
Go 1.27 added a portable, platform-agnostic SIMD interface inspired by Google Highway
articles.whyItMatters: Go developers writing performance-critical code can use vectorized CPU instructions without architecture-specific code.

articles.title: Samba 4.25 Released With Experimental SMB3 Persistent Handles
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Samba 4.25 is out, adding experimental SMB3 Persistent Handles so clients can reconnect after a server restart while keeping their file handles, though at a significant performance cost. It also adds a Ceph RGW VFS module, improved JSON audit logging, and AES as the default domain encryption type.
keyPoints: Experimental SMB3 Persistent Handles enable uninterrupted file access after server restarts
Persistent handles carry a significant performance cost from double storage per operation
New Ceph RGW VFS module exports Ceph Object Gateway buckets as SMB shares
articles.whyItMatters: Admins running Samba file services gain failover resilience and new Ceph integration, but must weigh the performance trade-off of persistent handles.

articles.title: Mageia 9 support ends September 30, users urged to upgrade to Mageia 10
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Mageia 9, released in August 2023, reaches end of support on September 30, 2026 and will stop receiving security fixes. Users can upgrade via the system tray update tool or command line, or do a clean install of Mageia 10.
keyPoints: Support ends September 30, 2026, three months after Mageia 10's June 30 release
Upgrade via system tray app, command line, or clean install; Live images cannot upgrade
Mageia 10 ships kernel 6.18 LTS, Plasma 6.5, GNOME 49, DNF 5
articles.whyItMatters: Mageia 9 users must upgrade before September 30 to keep receiving security updates.

articles.title: Samba 4.25 Released With New High-Availability and Clustering Features
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Samba 4.25 is out as the first stable release in the new series. Its headline addition is experimental SMB3 Persistent Handles for high-availability setups, plus a new Ceph RGW VFS module, safer cluster rolling upgrades, and stronger Kerberos encryption defaults.
keyPoints: Experimental SMB3 Persistent Handles let clients keep open files across server restarts
New vfs_ceph_rgw module exposes Ceph Object Gateway buckets as SMB shares
Kerberos defaults to AES encryption for domains at functional level 2008 or newer
articles.whyItMatters: Administrators running clustered Samba, Active Directory, or HA storage should review the release notes before upgrading.

articles.title: Installing Navidrome on Fedora Linux using Podman
articles.author: Nico Shetty
articles.brief: Fedora Magazine walks through running Navidrome, an open-source personal music streaming server, in Podman on Fedora. It covers pulling the official multi-arch image, SELinux contexts and ownership for data and music directories, and starting the service via podman-compose or the podman CLI.
keyPoints: Official deluan/navidrome image supports amd64, arm64, and arm/v6/v7
Set container_file_t SELinux context and UID 1000 ownership on Data and Music dirs
Run with podman-compose or podman run; configure via environment variables
articles.whyItMatters: Fedora users who want to self-host music streaming get a concrete, SELinux-aware Podman setup that also works on ARM devices like Raspberry Pi.

articles.title: Vicharak Axon-Lite: a tiny SBC with swappable interface modules
articles.author: Abhishek Prakash
articles.brief: Vicharak's Axon-Lite is a small ARM SBC built around the Rockchip RK3576 with a 6 TOPS NPU. Its hook is a modular connector letting users snap on voice, vision, sensing, or AI hub modules instead of stacking HATs. It's on pre-order at about $165-$200, shipping January 2027.
keyPoints: RK3576 SoC, 6 TOPS NPU, LPDDR5, eMMC/UFS/microSD storage
Four swappable modules shown: Voice Processing, Smart Sensing, AI Data Hub, AI Vision
Pre-order $165 (4GB) or $200 (8GB), ships January 2027
articles.whyItMatters: Makers and teams prototyping edge AI or vision projects get a modular alternative to stacking Raspberry Pi HATs, though the proprietary connector ties them to Vicharak's lineup.

articles.title: openEuler 24.03 LTS SP3 positions itself as the first open-source SuperPoD OS
articles.author: Edmar Pereira
articles.brief: openEuler's 24.03 LTS SP3 release targets AI clusters, using Huawei's UnifiedBus interconnect to let applications treat memory and accelerators across many nodes as one system. The project claims 30-50% performance gains in large-scale AI compute, and also ships Intelligence BooM, a full-stack AI layer, plus an…

articles.title: Linux Kernel Developers Consider Adding AGENTS.md To Guide AI/LLM Agents
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Sasha Levin has proposed adding an AGENTS.md file to the Linux kernel tree to steer AI coding agents toward kernel standards. The file links to the kernel README and assistant documentation; testing showed it fixed improper Signed-off-by and attribution tags. Some LKML members object over increased token consumption.

articles.title: Qualcomm Posts GPU Patches for Lower-Tier Snapdragon X2 'Mahua' SoC
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Qualcomm posted Linux kernel patches enabling the Adreno X2-85 GPU in its Mahua SoC, the codename for lower-tier 10 and 12 core Snapdragon X2 chips. The enablement requires only a few dozen lines of new graphics driver code and is now under review on the kernel mailing list.

articles.title: Ubuntu 26.10 adds Windows 11-style snap layout picker
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: Ubuntu 26.10 will show a layout picker that slides from the top of the screen when you drag a window, letting you snap apps into preset tile zones, similar to Windows 11. It was merged into the Tiling Assistant extension late in the cycle, past UI freeze. There is no off switch in Settings.

articles.title: ReactOS merges Wine 10.0-based DirectX stack overhaul, enabling hundreds more games
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: ReactOS has merged a major update bringing its DirectX stack to the Wine 10.0 state, replacing old hacks with 498k new lines of code. The work, led by developer Justin Miller, enables OpenGL and Vulkan translation for DirectX and reportedly unlocks hundreds of games.

articles.title: Firefox Smart Window Expands in Beta With Built-In AI Assistant
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Mozilla has detailed Smart Window, a third Firefox window type with a built-in AI assistant, now rolling out in beta to users in the US, Canada, and France. It offers tab grouping, page summarization, cross-tab comparison, and local 'Memories,' with a waitlist for other regions.

articles.title: Ubuntu 26.10 shows early gains on Intel Panther Lake Framework Laptop 13 Pro
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Phoronix reports Ubuntu 26.10 "Stonking Stingray" delivers out-of-the-box improvements over Ubuntu 26.04 LTS on Intel Core Ultra Series 3 "Panther Lake" hardware, tested on a Framework Laptop 13 Pro. Gains come from the Linux 7.3 kernel and newer Mesa, especially for Arc B390 Vulkan graphics.

articles.title: F-Droid 2.0: A new chapter for Android freedom
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: The F-Droid project has released version 2.0 of its official app, a complete redesign with better app discovery, improved search, and more useful categories. Key components were rewritten in Kotlin Compose and the UI updated to fit current Material Design patterns while keeping familiar interactions.

articles.title: File-notification attacks enable keystroke timing and KDE clickjacking on Linux
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: Graz University of Technology researchers disclosed file-notification attacks affecting Android, Linux, macOS, and Windows. On Linux, inotify can be abused for inter-keystroke timing attacks without file read access, and monitoring pkexec enables clickjacking of Polkit prompts on KDE 5 and 6.

articles.title: Ubuntu 26.10 beta delayed by a week, now due 1 October
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: Canonical has pushed the Ubuntu 26.10 beta back from 24 September to 1 October, citing unforeseen infrastructure issues. The final stable release on 15 October 2026 is unaffected. Testers can use daily builds in the meantime.

articles.title: COSMIC Epoch 1.9 Released With New Image Viewer and On-Screen Keyboard
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: System76's Rust-based COSMIC desktop environment released Epoch 1.9, adding COSMIC Viewer, a native image viewer with built-in editing, and COSMIC OSK, an on-screen keyboard. The release also overhauls the COSMIC Store and updates the compositor, with downloads available on GitHub.

articles.title: COSMIC Desktop 1.9 Adds COSMIC Viewer Image App and On-Screen Keyboard
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: System76 released COSMIC Desktop 1.9, adding the COSMIC Viewer image editor/viewer and COSMIC OSK on-screen keyboard for touch and gamepad input. The release also overhauls the COSMIC Store visually, fixes numerous UI bugs, and improves COSMIC Files and Settings.

articles.title: AMD Posts GCC Compiler Patches For AVX10V1AUX ISA Support
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: AMD compiler engineers posted initial GCC patches enabling AVX10V1AUX, the auxiliary update to AVX10.1 under the ACE AI Compute Extensions initiative. The patches add infrastructure, reuse AVX10.2 built-ins and CONVERT intrinsics, and are enabled via -mavx10v1aux.

articles.title: Ubuntu Moves Kernel SRUs to a Two-Week Cycle Driven by AI Bug Hunting
articles.author: Sourav Rudra
articles.brief: Canonical is replacing its split kernel update tracks with a single two-week SRU cycle, with cycles overlapping weekly so a kernel release ships every week. The change responds to LLMs and AI agents discovering kernel vulnerabilities faster than humans can, aiming for workarounds within 24-48 hours of a public CVE.

articles.title: COSMIC 1.9 Desktop Environment Released with COSMIC Viewer and COSMIC OSK
articles.brief: System76's COSMIC 1.9 desktop environment is out, adding the COSMIC Viewer image viewer and COSMIC OSK on-screen keyboard apps. Further details were not available in the teaser.

articles.title: [$] Listening to the radio with Rust
articles.author: daroc
articles.brief: At RustConf 2026 in Montreal, Thomas Eckert presented his hobby of decoding radio transmissions with Rust using a cheap hardware dongle. He covered the math behind software-defined radio and demonstrated AM/FM reception plus decoding aircraft transponder signals, with slides and code on GitHub.

articles.title: The Kernel Report 2026 edition
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: After a two-year hiatus, Jonathan Corbet presented an updated Kernel Report at Kernel Recipes, covering the kernel community's state amid accelerated change and its future direction. Video of the talk is available on YouTube.

articles.title: Fedora discussion floats replacing LibreOffice with Collabora Office by default
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: A Fedora Discourse thread proposing Collabora Office replace LibreOffice as Fedora Workstation's default office suite has drawn lively debate. Supporters cite LibreOffice's "very ancient" UI; critics raise licensing, Flatpak-only distribution, and paid-service concerns. No formal change proposal has reached FESCo.

articles.title: KDE Plasma 6.8 Beta 2 Released With Union Theming Engine Maturing
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: KDE Plasma 6.8 Beta 2, the final beta before the stable release, is out for testing. Its Union theming system now covers QtWidgets apps like Dolphin and Kate, and a KWin Wayland memory leak is fixed. Plasma 6.8.0 stable is due 14 October.

articles.title: Security updates for Thursday
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: LWN's daily roundup lists security updates issued by eight Linux distributions on September 23-24, 2026. AlmaLinux, Oracle, Fedora, Ubuntu, Debian, SUSE, and Mageia patched packages including kernels, firefox, postgresql, openssh, and container tooling.

articles.title: AlmaLinux launches certification portal and alma-certify self-certification app
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: AlmaLinux expanded its two-year-old hardware certification program to cover third-party software and released a rewritten self-certification app plus a public catalog at catalog.almalinux.org. The app, installable via dnf as alma-certify, runs certification tests in under ten minutes.

articles.title: FOSS Weekly #26.39: Snapdragon X2 Linux Support, Ubuntu 26.10, Portainer Goes Closed Source
articles.author: Abhishek Prakash
articles.brief: This week's Linux roundup covers Qualcomm's early Snapdragon X2 developer preview for Linux, Ubuntu 26.10's smarter low-memory handling, and Portainer moving its 3.0 rebuild to closed source. Also featured: Valve open-sourcing its Lepton Android layer, Mozilla's Mistral partnership, and Signal testing numberless…

articles.title: Linux Kernel Adds TAINT_FORCED_BIND to Flag Impractical Fuzzing Bot Bug Reports
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Greg Kroah-Hartman is adding a new kernel taint flag, TAINT_FORCED_BIND, set whenever a driver's sysfs bind/unbind files are written. The goal is to mark bug reports caused by fuzzing bots like Syzbot that bind arbitrary devices to drivers, creating impractical combinations no real user would hit.

articles.title: Mir 2.30 Released: Rust Compiler Now Required, Public Roadmap Published
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Canonical released Mir 2.30, its Wayland compositor library, now mandating a Rust compiler for builds as it uses Rust evdev input code and targets Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. The release adds wl_fixes protocol support, bug fixes, and a public roadmap covering plans like an all-Rust compositor and a new rendering pipeline.

articles.title: What's Up Docker 9.0 Released With SQLite Backend, RBAC, and API Tokens
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: What's Up Docker 9.0, a container update monitoring tool, switches its persistence layer from LokiJS to SQLite with Drizzle ORM and automatic migrations. It adds role-based access control, personal API tokens, expanded OIDC support, and removes anonymous access, making authentication mandatory.

articles.title: Canonical Releases Mir 2.30 with wl_fixes Wayland Protocol Support
articles.brief: Canonical has released Mir 2.30, adding support for the wl_fixes Wayland protocol, a typed wrapper for wl_array, and a new command in the workshop tooling, among other changes.

articles.title: Fwupd 2.1.8 Adds New Hardware Support and Firmware Update Fixes
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Fwupd 2.1.8 is out, adding support for new docks, fingerprint sensors, and other hardware alongside fixes for crashes, memory leaks, and firmware recovery. New features include a bootupd notification plugin and RSA-3072 signature verification for Lenovo accessories.

articles.title: Fwupd 2.1.8 Linux Firmware Updater Released with Support for More Devices
articles.brief: Fwupd 2.1.8 is now available for download, adding support for new devices including the ASUS GX5407 and Elan PID 0CB6. Only a teaser was available, so further changes are unknown.

articles.title: Fwupd 2.1.8 Released With New Hardware Support From ASUS, Lenovo & Others
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Fwupd 2.1.8 is out, adding support for new devices including the ASUS ProArt P16, Lenovo ThinkPad Thunderbolt 4 Dock Gen 2, and various MediaTek, MaxLinear, and PixArt hardware. It also adds a plug-in to notify bootupd of ESP changes, RSA-3072 signature verification for Lenovo hardware, and bug fixes.

articles.title: "slab_tiny" Boot Option Proposed For Tiny Linux Systems With Very Limited RAM
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: SUSE's Vlastimil Babka posted an RFC patch series replacing the CONFIG_SLUB_TINY Kconfig option with a boot-time "slab_tiny" parameter, simplifying the kernel's small-memory slab allocator handling. It targets embedded systems with 16MB of RAM or less.

articles.title: Linux 7.4 DRM gains HDMI 2.0 helpers via drm-misc-next
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: This week's drm-misc-next pull for Linux 7.4 adds new HDMI 2.0 infrastructure to the DRM core, including scrambler support and SCDC helper code. The work comes from Collabora's Cristian Ciocaltea, who is enabling HDMI 2.0 on the Synopsys DW HDMI QP TX controller used in Rockchip SoCs, and will also serve VC4 and…

articles.title: PhotoPrism AI-Powered Photos App Gets Better Face Detection
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Self-hosted photo app PhotoPrism released an update with new face detection and embedding models that catch more faces, including smaller ones in group shots. Existing libraries must opt in via a new `photoprism faces migrate` command.

articles.title: Qualcomm Announces Snapdragon X2 Linux Developer Preview
articles.author: Sourav Rudra
articles.brief: Qualcomm released an early Linux developer preview for Snapdragon X2 laptops, targeting kernel developers and distro maintainers rather than end users. It pairs a Debian 13 userspace with a custom kernel and pushes drivers toward mainline instead of out-of-tree patches.

articles.title: GNOME 50.5 Released With Numerous Bug and Security Fixes
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: GNOME 50.5 is a maintenance update for the old-stable GNOME 50 series, now that GNOME 51 is current, updating 22 components. It brings bug fixes across Shell, Mutter, GTK, and GDM plus security fixes in GVfs, librsvg, and Epiphany. Users on GNOME 50 are advised to update via their distribution.

articles.title: How to test Ubuntu's AI dictation tool Myna ahead of its official release
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: Canonical's local AI speech-to-text tool Myna isn't officially ready, but its components are available to test on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS and 26.10. Installation requires a PPA settings app, a Myna snap, and a local Whisper or Parakeet AI model, with an on-screen HUD via a GNOME Shell extension on 26.10.

articles.title: openKylin 3.0 Released with Deep AI Integration and Linux Kernel 7.0
articles.author: Abhishek Prakash
articles.brief: openKylin 3.0 ships Linux kernel 7.0, UKUI 4.24, and a built-in AI agent framework called KylinBot with its Xiao K assistant, which can control system settings via text or voice. The release also adds Rust-based replacement utilities and gesture controls; the AI skills documentation is currently only in Chinese.

articles.title: Ubuntu moves kernel security updates to a two-week cycle amid AI-driven surge in CVEs
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: Canonical is switching Ubuntu kernel updates from a 4/2 schedule to a unified two-week SRU cycle, effectively shipping fixes weekly. The change responds to an 'explosion' of vulnerabilities being found with AI models and agents.

articles.title: Wireshark 4.6.9 Packet Analyzer Fixes 19 Security Vulnerabilities
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Wireshark 4.6.9, a maintenance release of the network protocol analyzer, patches 19 vulnerabilities, mostly crashes in protocol dissectors and file parsers. The most serious, CVE-2026-96419 in profile import, could allow code execution.

articles.title: Original Windows Task Manager dev builds TMOG, a cross-platform system monitor
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: David Plummer, who wrote the original Windows Task Manager, has released TMOG, a cross-platform system monitor built with Claude Code from a 100+ page spec. The Linux version uses Qt 6 atop a shared C++ core, and is available as a Deb, AppImage, or binary. Some features sit behind a $39.95 Pro tier.

articles.title: Wireshark 4.6.9 Updates Protocol and Capture File Support, Fixes More Bugs
articles.brief: Wireshark 4.6.9 is now available for download, bringing updated protocol and capture file support alongside various bug and security fixes.

articles.title: Debian Inference Portal offers free AI/LLM inferencing to Debian developers
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Following Debian's vote to allow responsible generative AI use, the Debian Inference Portal has launched, giving contributors free self-service access to LLM inferencing. Funded by Scaleway, it offers DeepSeek V4 Flash and GLM-5.2 models via an API for use with editors and AI tooling.

articles.title: Qualcomm Showcases Linux on Snapdragon X2 Laptops, Developer Preview Announced
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: At its Snapdragon Summit, Qualcomm announced an early developer preview of Linux for Snapdragon X2 laptops, using a custom kernel with a Debian 13 user-space. HP, ASUS, and HUMAIN plan Linux support on X2 devices in the first half of 2027.

articles.title: Lemonade 2026.39.1/2026.40 RC Fix APU Model Streaming, Drop OpenMOSS ROCm
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: AMD's Lemonade local AI server released 2026.39.1 and a 2026.40 RC. The RC fixes streaming models on AMD APUs by checking the GTT pool instead of the fixed vRAM carve-out, and removes the OpenMOSS ROCm back-end for running about 40x slower than Vulkan. 2026.39.1 adds configurable vRAM auto-eviction.

articles.title: Debian-Based SparkyLinux 2026.09 “Tiamat” Introduces Sparky Labwc Edition
articles.brief: SparkyLinux 2026.09 “Tiamat” is available for download, shipping Linux kernel 7.2, a new Sparky Labwc edition, and the latest Debian “Forky” Testing updates.

articles.title: SparkyLinux 2026.09 Released With Kernel 7.2 and New Labwc Edition
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: SparkyLinux 2026.09 "Tiamat" refreshes the semi-rolling branch on a Debian "Forky" Testing base with kernel 7.2.6 and updated desktop images. The main addition is a new Labwc MinimalGUI edition, a lightweight Wayland compositor setup installed from the command line.

articles.title: Ubuntu Kernels Move to Weekly Releases for Faster CVE Fixes
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Canonical is replacing Ubuntu's four-week SRU and two-week security kernel cycles with overlapping two-week cycles, yielding a new kernel release every week. Testing is not shortened; one kernel certifies while the next is prepared.

articles.title: git-bug 0.11 Adds a Full Web UI for Issues and Code Browsing
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: git-bug 0.11, the first release in 16 months of the distributed bug tracker that stores issues inside Git, rewrites its web UI from scratch and adds a built-in code browser. The backend gains Git browsing via GraphQL, the search index shrinks dramatically with Bleve v2, and some breaking changes apply.

articles.title: Konveyor Brings Niri-Like Scrolling Tiling to KDE Plasma
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Konveyor is a new open-source project that adds Niri-inspired scrolling column tiling to KDE Plasma as a KWin effect, leaving panels, widgets, and other desktop features intact. It supports multi-monitor layouts, tabbed columns, gestures, and an optional launcher. It requires Plasma 6.4 or later on Wayland.

articles.title: Gravity Linux Is a New Fedora Remix for Apple Silicon Designed to Eventually Disappear
articles.author: Sourav Rudra
articles.brief: Gravity Linux is a Fedora Remix for Apple Silicon Macs, forked from Asahi Linux over LLM contribution policy, shipping KDE Plasma on Wayland. Its first alpha runs on the M4 Mac mini with working hardware-accelerated graphics. The project's goal is to upstream all driver work, then sunset itself.

articles.title: [$] Ideas on modernizing the open-source desktop
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: At Akademy 2026, veteran UI/UX designer Scott Jenson urged open-source projects to experiment beyond the classic WIMP desktop model. He argued KDE and its community should take the lead on desktop design innovation.

articles.title: KeePassXC 2.8 Beta 1 Brings Qt 6, Wayland Auto-Type, and Security Fixes
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: KeePassXC released the first beta of version 2.8, a major update that ports the password manager from Qt 5 to Qt 6 and adds remote database synchronization. Linux users gain Auto-Type on Wayland and Polkit-based Quick Unlock. The beta also patches several low-to-moderate severity vulnerabilities affecting 2.7.x.

articles.title: Intel Open-Sources DXVK-IGDEXT for Faster Arc Gaming on Linux
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Intel engineers have open-sourced DXVK-IGDEXT, an igdext64.dll for Wine/DXVK that exposes Intel D3D11 Graphics Extensions—UAV overlap, MultiDrawIndirect, depth bounds—by forwarding them to DXVK's native implementation.

articles.title: Systemd v262 released
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: Systemd v262 has been released. Notable additions include building systemd as a single statically linked binary for small containers, support for the kernel coredump socket protocol from Linux 6.17, and OpenSSL 4 support.

articles.title: Local AI Weekly #3: cheap frontier AI won't last, plus local tools and model news
articles.author: Abhishek Prakash
articles.brief: This newsletter issue argues that cheap, generous AI subscriptions are a hook before prices rise, making local models a safer bet. It also covers open-source agent inboxes from Cloudflare and AWS, new tools like OpenPencil and Kalypta, and Microsoft's Rust rewrite of the Copilot runtime.

articles.title: Critical Radicle protocol flaws expose traffic and enable node impersonation
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: Radicle disclosed two critical network-protocol flaws: traffic lacks expected confidentiality, and broken peer authentication lets attackers spoof Node IDs to read private repositories. Combined, an on-path attacker can observe allow-listed Node IDs, read exchanges, and fetch repositories; no setting or allow-list…

articles.title: Benchmarking Java Performance Of JDK 8 Through OpenJDK 27
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Phoronix benchmarked every major OpenJDK release from 8 through the new 27 on a Threadripper 9980X workstation running Fedora 44. Tests used official binaries with default settings across DaCapoBench and Renaissance suites, though some benchmarks had issues with pre-OpenJDK 11 versions.

articles.title: KeePassXC 2.8 Beta Brings Auto-Type on Wayland and Qt 6 Port
articles.brief: KeePassXC 2.8 is now in public beta, adding Auto-Type support on Wayland, quick unlock on Linux, and a long-awaited port to Qt 6.

articles.title: Critical WordPress RCE vulnerability announced
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: A critical vulnerability in WordPress's get_page_template() function could allow unauthenticated remote-code execution in limited circumstances. Fixes are available for the latest branch and backported to 4.7; the ClassicPress fork is also affected but has no update yet.

articles.title: Security updates for Wednesday
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: LWN's daily roundup of distribution security advisories covering AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, Red Hat, SUSE, and Ubuntu. Notable updates include kernel fixes for Fedora, SUSE, and Ubuntu, plus patches for chromium, firefox, openssh, sudo, and bind.

articles.title: NTFS-3G 2026.9.18 released with heap overflow and DoS security fixes
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: NTFS-3G 2026.9.18, the FUSE-based NTFS driver, fixes multiple heap buffer overflows, possible heap corruption, and a denial-of-service vector. It also addresses an ntfsresize issue with stale $MFTMirr data and is available from GitHub.

articles.title: NTFS-3G 2026.9.18 NTFS Driver for Linux Released with Security and Bug Fixes
articles.brief: NTFS-3G 2026.9.18, the driver for handling NTFS partitions on Linux-based systems, is now available for download. The release brings various security and bug fixes.

articles.title: Qualcomm Posts Open-Source GPU Driver Patches For Adreno 850 One Day After Announcement
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: One day after announcing the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, Qualcomm engineers posted initial Linux kernel patches bringing up its Adreno 850 GPU in the MSM driver. The series also adds the similar Adreno 845 'Maili' GPU, which lacks the A850's new MALU matrix core. Mesa and linux-firmware support are promised soon.

articles.title: AMD Upstreams AVX10_V2_AUX Support Into LLVM Clang 24
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: AMD's AVX10_V2_AUX support has been merged into LLVM 24, exposed via the new -mavx10v2aux Clang flag. The instructions add data-type conversion to FP4/FP6, OCP microscaling formats, and new rounding modes as part of the Intel/AMD AI Compute Extensions. LLVM/Clang 24.1 stable is expected around March.

articles.title: Linux 7.3 Reverts Logitech Bolt Receiver HID++ Support After Bug Reports
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Linux 7.3 added Logitech Bolt receiver support to hid-logitech-dj with HID++, but it caused scroll-wheel and settings bugs with Logitech mice. Benjamin Tissoires has queued a revert to the generic HID driver, dropping HID++ functionality until the issues can be properly addressed.

articles.title: Sublime Text Build 4213 Adds Python 3.14 Runtime and File Icon Themes
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Sublime Text Build 4213 upgrades the plugin runtime from Python 3.8 to 3.14, adds file icon themes and an open_terminal command, and speeds up Git status and multi-file saving. It also ships a rewritten C# syntax definition plus Linux fixes for modal dialogs, KDE input, and Wayland tab dragging.

articles.title: NVIDIA 595.104.02 Linux Graphics Driver Released with Better Wayland Support
articles.brief: NVIDIA 595.104.02 for Linux is available, bringing fixes for bugs and crashes to improve driver stability and reliability, plus better Wayland support.

articles.title: FreeRDP 3.32 Adds Microsoft Entra Integration on Linux
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: FreeRDP 3.32.0 ships with Microsoft Entra/Azure integration for the SDL and xfreerdp clients, beta RemoteApp (RAIL) support on X11 and Wayland, and a reworked FFmpeg-based hardware video pipeline. The release also hardens security, including a default-deny certificate policy on the proxy side.

articles.title: Installing Fedora 45 on Stratis storage
articles.author: Vojtěch Trefný
articles.brief: Fedora 45's Anaconda installer adds Stratis as a storage option. In the Web UI, Stratis layouts are built manually via the integrated Cockpit storage module; kickstart gains full support with a stratis autopart type and new stratispool and stratisfs commands.

articles.title: Local AI Jargon Quiz: Do You Know All These Buzzwords?
articles.author: Abhishek Prakash
articles.brief: A ten-question quiz tests how well you understand common local AI terms like tokens, harness, and quantization, with a correct description per term. It's aimed at people who run models locally with tools like Ollama or llama.cpp.

articles.title: Nouveau driver gets patches for HDMI Deep Color support
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: New patches posted to the dri-devel mailing list add HDMI Deep Color support to Nouveau, the open-source NVIDIA Linux kernel driver, enabling 10, 12, or 16 bits per color channel. The patches currently support only RGB, and 16-bit output is untested on capable displays.

articles.title: Drew DeVault: Hacker News's right-wing bias flows from Y Combinator itself
articles.author: September
articles.brief: Drew DeVault argues that Hacker News systematically suppresses progressive views through flagging, automated moderation, and its moderators, citing flagged comments critical of Musk's Grok. He traces the bias to Y Combinator's leaders — Paul Graham, Sam Altman, and Garry Tan — and their politics and associations.

articles.title: OpenShot video editor now officially available as a snap
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: OpenShot's official snap package went live on the Canonical Snap Store on 22 September, installable on all supported Ubuntu releases. It eases installation and brings newer versions to older LTS users, though sandbox permissions for microphone, camera, and removable media must be granted manually.

articles.title: Linux 7.2 vs. Linux 7.3 Shows A Few Improvements With AMD Strix Halo
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Phoronix benchmarked Linux 7.3 against 7.2 on an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 Strix Halo Framework Desktop after Ubuntu 26.10 switched kernels. Most real-world workloads were unchanged, but NUMA performance improved significantly, network latency dropped slightly, and a few graphics and micro-benchmarks saw small gains.

articles.title: KDE Picks Enterprise, Documentation, and Styling as New Goals
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: KDE has chosen three community goals for 2026–2028: making Plasma viable for enterprise and managed deployments, overhauling its fragmented documentation, and building a next-generation styling system via the Ocean design system and Union theming engine.

articles.title: Ubuntu wiki gets its first overhaul in 16 years
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: Canonical has launched a rebuilt Ubuntu Wiki, its first major update since 2010, now running on MediaWiki. The new wiki is smaller and aimed at Ubuntu users rather than contributors, replacing an aging Python 2 stack with security vulnerabilities.

articles.title: PeppermintOS switches from Xorg to XLibre, avoiding Wayland
articles.author: Abhishek Prakash
articles.brief: PeppermintOS is replacing the stalled xorg-server with XLibre, an X11 fork, in its upcoming ISO refreshes, and says it has no plans to move to Wayland. Testing has gone well so far, but XLibre is controversial: Artix Linux adopted it as default, then reverted after heavy bug reports and harassment of a developer.

articles.title: Survey: Organizations increasingly adopt OpenSearch for AI workloads, not just search
articles.author: Sourav Rudra
articles.brief: A Linux Foundation Research and OpenSearch Software Foundation report, based on 294 respondents surveyed in May 2026, finds OpenSearch awareness at 89% and production deployments doubled to 36% in two years. Among users, 62% run AI workloads on it, with cost and vendor independence driving adoption.

articles.title: NetBSD 10.2 Released With New Hardware Support and Security Fixes
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: The NetBSD Project has released NetBSD 10.2, the second point release in the still-supported NetBSD 10 stable branch. It adds hardware support including Realtek RTL8126 5Gbps Ethernet, fixes security issues in IPFilter and TCP timestamps, and updates OpenSSL to 3.0.21 and Xorg to 21.1.24.

articles.title: Compiling the kernel with gccrs
articles.author: daroc
articles.brief: Talks at RustConf 2026 and Kangrejos covered the status of gccrs, the Rust frontend for GCC, with a focus on compiling the Linux kernel. The project is making good progress, but the compiler remains far from usable for that goal.

articles.title: Security updates for Tuesday
articles.author: jake
articles.brief: LWN's daily roundup lists security updates from AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, Slackware, SUSE, and Ubuntu. Fedora 45 ships a large coordinated update touching ffmpeg, chromium, and many multimedia packages; Ubuntu fixes include the kernel, OpenJDK, glib2.0, and expat across multiple LTS releases.

articles.title: AMD BC-250 Linux support expands with PSP secure processor enablement patches
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: New kernel patches enable the AMD PSP Secure Processor on the BC-250, a cut-down PlayStation 5 APU board originally sold for crypto mining. The three-patch series updates the AMD CCP driver so the board's secure processor works for encryption tasks under Linux.

articles.title: Igalia Celebrates 25 Years of Linux and Open-Source Contributions
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Worker-owned consultancy Igalia, founded in September 2001 by University of A Coruña engineers, marks 25 years of open-source work. Now nearly 200 people, it contributes to the Linux kernel, WebKit, Chromium, Servo, Mesa, GStreamer, and LLVM, with recent projects for Valve and others.

articles.title: Linux perf script overhauled as fast Python C module
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: A 49-patch series from Google engineer Ian Rogers replaces perf's embedded Python/Perl scripting with a standalone Python C extension module, cutting overhead and build dependencies. One script that took 3.7 seconds now runs in 0.1 seconds.

articles.title: Kernel prepatch 7.3-rc4
articles.author: jake
articles.brief: Linus Torvalds has released the fourth release candidate of kernel 7.3, remarking that it is a large one. Only a teaser was available, so further details are not included here.

articles.title: Linux 7.3-rc4 Released: More Fixes Caught By LLMs, But Nothing Too Scary
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Linus Torvalds released Linux 7.3-rc4, a larger-than-usual rc with fixes spread across drivers, filesystems, and networking, many flagged by LLM-based defect hunting. Notable merges include x86 fixes, new XPad game controller support, two Btrfs bug fixes, and a fix for silent user-space data loss present since 2023.

articles.title: Important x86 Fixes Merged Ahead Of Linux 7.3-rc4
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: A batch of x86/x86_64 fixes landed in Linux 7.3 Git ahead of 7.3-rc4. They block problematic Intel Granite Rapids microcode that could cause machine check exceptions, fix Intel FRED on Panther Lake crashing games under Wine/Steam Play, and disable APX register use in -march=native kernel builds.

articles.title: Gzip 1.15 Released, Fixing Bugs Present Since Its Inception
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Gzip 1.15 is out, following version 1.14 from April 2025, with over a hundred commits focused on bug fixes. Several bugs existed since the tool's beginning, including a race that could remove the wrong file, a buffer overflow in LZH decompression, and use of uninitialized memory.

articles.title: KDE's 2026-2028 Goals: Enterprise Support, Better Docs, Next-Gen Styling
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: At KDE Akademy 2026 in Graz, KDE announced its three community-voted goals for the next two years: improving Plasma for enterprise deployments, overhauling documentation, and building a next-generation styling system via the Ocean design project and Union theming engine.

articles.title: Starling 0.5 desktop adds optional walkable 3D waterfront city mode
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Starling, the Swift-written Wayland desktop developed largely with Claude Code, released version 0.5 with an optional 3D desktop mode rendering a walkable waterfront city where apps remain real windows. The release also adds Windows support via WSL2 with RDP display mode.

articles.title: Vulkan 1.4.363 Released With New VK_INTEL_device_info Extension
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Vulkan 1.4.363 is out with spec clarifications, fixes, and multi-instance VUs for DMA-BUF external memory. Its headline addition is VK_INTEL_device_info, an Intel vendor extension that exposes the graphics IP block version of Intel GPUs to applications.

articles.title: AMD Strix Halo Shows Performance Gains on Ubuntu 26.10, Especially with amd64v3
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Phoronix benchmarked a Framework Desktop with a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 Strix Halo chip on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS versus an Ubuntu 26.10 daily ISO, plus an amd64v3 package build. Ubuntu 26.10 reportedly performs better than 26.04 LTS, with extra out-of-the-box gains from the experimental x86_64-v3 packages.

articles.title: Fedora CoreOS 45 Test Week starts September 21
articles.author: Lukáš Růžička
articles.brief: The Fedora CoreOS and QA teams are running a Test Week starting September 21, 2026, inviting the community to test Fedora CoreOS based on Fedora 45 before it reaches testing and stable streams. Participants download test images, follow provided test cases, and report results on the wiki page.

articles.title: Fedora Linux Asahi Remix 45 Beta brings Fedora 45 to Apple Silicon
articles.author: Davide Cavalca
articles.brief: Fedora Asahi Remix 45 Beta is out, bringing Fedora Linux 45 Beta to Apple Silicon Macs ahead of general availability in about a month. It is the first Remix release with out-of-the-box support for M3, M3 Pro, and M3 Max systems, though M3 GPU acceleration awaits a future Mesa update.
